Patients in regional and rural settings are highly willing partners in developing skills of junior medical students. In fact, our study found that patients in these areas were more involved in patient consultations than previously reported for urban students. This suggests that patients from regional and rural settings may be interested in participating in community-based medical education programs.

To enhance their involvement, it is essential to provide a supportive environment where they feel comfortable sharing their experiences and learning from junior medical students. Community-based medical education programs should also address the unique challenges faced by patients in these regions, such as limited access to healthcare services and lack of quality care.

By involving patients in the development of skills and knowledge, community-based medical education can lead to improved health outcomes for patients in regional and rural Australia. This approach not only enhances patient engagement but also acknowledges the critical role that patients play in shaping the future of healthcare delivery in these areas.

In summary, patients from regional and rural settings are eager participants in the new wave of community-based medical education in Australia, and programs should prioritize their involvement to maximize benefits for public health.
